newsitem.title: NORWAY: Swedish Pepsi deal seen good for Orkla.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Pepsi deal seen good for Orkla.

text.p: Analysts took a positive view on Tuesday on the deal between Norwegian-Swedish beverage maker Pripps Ringnes and PepsiCo on production, distribution and sales of Pepsi-Cola and 7UP in Sweden as of 2001.
"I would be surprised if a similar agreement is not soon entered into for Norway," one analyst said.
The companies have started preliminary discussions about possible cooperation in Norway but have so far not reached an agreement, Pripps Ringnes said.
"The contract with Coca-Cola CO was seen as bad so Orkla should be able to profit as much if not more on the PepsiCo deal," another analyst said.
Coca-Cola and Pripps Ringnes last January signed a final agreement to end the two companies' cooperation.
Orkla's A share was up 13.50 crowns at 559.50 crowns at 1015GMT

Pripps Ringnes said in a statement on Monday that it would get the full responsibility for the brand names of Pepsi-Cola and 7UP of January 1, 2001, when PepsiCo's deal with its current Swedish partner expires.
PepsiCo is now cooperating with Swedish family-controlled beverage company Spendrups in Sweden.
Analysts said a possible negative result of the PepsiCo deal was that Spendrup might look for an international partner, which could pose a threat to Pripps Ringnes in its beer business.
